reviews.one_line_contribution: The claim that a large share of agent-memory harm is caused by *when* retrieved experience is seen rather than by its content or volume — operationalized as commit-then-consult (draft and log an answer with no memory, then revise against the identical k=7 items at matched deciding-pass tokens) — plus the risky corollary that GEPA-optimized instructions make memory-first injection *more* harmful because a better instruction is a better prior to abandon.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal concedes CoVe and Astute-RAG and implements them (A5), but it never engages the context-vs-parametric knowledge-conflict line, which is where its actual mechanism already lives: Xie et al., 'Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth' (ICLR 2024), shows LLMs flip to coherent external evidence and that eliciting the model's own answer before showing the evidence systematically changes flip behaviour; Zhou et al.'s context-faithful prompting (opinion-based/counterfactual framing) manipulates exactly the 'is this a command or evidence' distinction; GenRead (Yu et al. 2023) is generate-before-retrieve. Together these establish commitment-order-before-evidence as a known lever with known effects. That does not fully collide — none of them is in an agentic loop with an ExpeL-style procedural bank, none decomposes fixes vs. breaks, and none touches instruction optimization — but it does mean the ordering half of the paper is a domain transplant of a documented effect, not a new mechanism. Novelty then rests almost entirely on P4, and the proposal's own refutation clause concedes that if A5 ties A2, nothing but P4 survives.
reviews.strongest_objection: Assay sensitivity. The pilot the whole proposal is built on reports the bank fixing *zero* items and breaking six to seven. If the frozen bank behaves the same way (and the write path is unchanged from ExpeL-style distillation), then A0 dominates every memory condition by construction, the P2 non-inferiority test has a 2-point margin around a reference effect of ~0 — a vacuous test that any inert method passes — and 'A2 halves breaks' becomes indistinguishable from 'A2 taught the agent to ignore the bank', which is the outcome the proposal itself calls 'no better than not retrieving.' The dev precheck (≥4% wrong→right) is explicitly 'reported, not used as a gate in silence', i.e. not a gate at all, so the grid can run and produce a headline that is uninterpretable. Second, the two mechanism arms are confounded in ways that let the competing account explain a positive result: G3 changes slot AND removes directive content from the memory slot ('the memory slot retains episodic residue only'), so G3's memory slot carries fewer tokens than A1's — that is A7's volume remedy wearing a slot costume, and P5's 'redundancy' would then be a token-count result. Relatedly, I* is presumably much longer and more specific than the base instruction, so G1 vs. A1 differs in total context length: the token-matching the paper's whole rhetoric depends on is enforced in the memory slot and abandoned in the instruction slot, precisely in the arm carrying the sharpest claim. Third, P4's endpoint is unnormalized: breaks are items correct in the reference and wrong under treatment, so if I* raises G0 accuracy at all, more items become eligible to break and the DiD rises with no change in per-item override hazard — a base-rate artifact that would produce the predicted ≥1.5× ratio for free. The most likely interleaving is the fatal one: A7 ≈ A5 ≈ A2 ≈ A0 on breaks, fixes ≈ 0 everywhere, G1−G0 inflated by G0's higher accuracy — at which point the paper's recommendation is 'retrieve less, or don't retrieve', for 2× the calls.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Make the dev precheck a hard pre-registered gate with a declared fallback (e.g. gold-trajectory-seeded or task-matched bank) and state in advance that a ≈0-fix bank reframes the paper as 'memory is net-negative in this setting', not as 'our fix preserves fixes'; a non-inferiority margin must be smaller than the reference effect it guards. (2) Report breaks as a hazard conditional on reference-correct instances (breaks / #correct-in-reference) for every fix/break table, and re-state P4 on that normalized quantity — otherwise the interaction is confounded with G0's accuracy. (3) Repair G3 so that slot is varied without varying volume: keep memory-slot token count and item count identical to A1 (pad with the episodic residue, or duplicate the directives into the instruction while leaving the memory slot untouched), and add an instruction control matched to I* in length and directiveness but not GEPA-optimized, so P4 tests optimization rather than instruction verbosity. (4) Sample ≥3 GEPA instruction draws (the Pareto frontier is already there and this is nearly free relative to the 22.5k-episode budget) — a single I* makes P4 an n=1 result the proposal itself flags but does not fix. (5) Add the directiveness manipulation rather than only the directiveness regression: minimal-edit imperative→declarative rewrites of the *same* items at matched tokens. That is the clean, cheap causal test of the paper's own mechanism and it is currently the only one missing.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. (a) A length- and directiveness-matched *unoptimized* instruction in the coupling arm (call it I_len: hand-written or a mid-run GEPA candidate, same token count and imperative density as I*, no training signal). Without it, P4 cannot separate 'the optimizer made the prior stronger' from 'the instruction slot got longer and more imperative', and G1 vs. A1 is not token-matched at all. (b) A placebo-memory arm: k=7 topically plausible but non-applicable items at matched tokens. The override signature (P6, >25% first-action divergence with sub-baseline conditional accuracy) is currently consistent with generic distraction by any instruction-shaped text; without a placebo there is no evidence that the agent is abandoning a correct plan *because the retrieved item is directive about this task*. A6's query-conditioned rewriting does not serve either role.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average and clearly executed — it names ~12 specific recent preprints with IDs, gives a per-item collide/no-collide verdict, concedes CoVe as the structural ancestor, and converts two named competitors (Astute-RAG→A5, MemHarness→A6) into run conditions rather than prose distinctions. I found no 2026 agent-memory preprint in the listed set that already makes the ordering claim, and P4 does look unclaimed. But the check is lopsided in exactly the direction that matters: it sweeps the 2026 agentic-memory axis thoroughly and never sweeps the context-vs-parametric knowledge-conflict axis (Xie et al. ICLR 2024; context-faithful prompting; generate-before-retrieve), which is where 'elicit the model's own answer before showing conflicting evidence' is already an established manipulation with published effects — that is a stronger threat to the ordering half than anything in cluster (3) or (4). The proposal also self-reports that the OpenReview/ACL-EMNLP proceedings sweep for ordering-ablation appendices was never run, and concedes 'a nontrivial probability' that draft-then-consult appears as an appendix ablation somewhere; and P4's unclaimed status rests on 'no paper we found asks', an absence-of-evidence from a search the proposal itself calls budget-exhausted. Honest, but the honesty documents the gap rather than closing it, and the unsearched region is the one containing the closest prior art.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That agent-memory harm is caused by commitment order rather than injected volume or item content, tested by a token-matched commit-then-consult arm (A2) plus a slot-routing arm (G3) and one genuinely risky prediction: GEPA-optimized instructions should make memory-first injection more harmful (G1 vs A1), not less.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal names CoVe, Astute/Madam-RAG, Self-Refine and Speculative RAG, but misses the cluster that most threatens it: the knowledge-conflict RAG literature. Xie et al., Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth (ICLR 2024), directly studies whether an LLM abandons a prior answer when shown conflicting external evidence, and reports that eliciting the model's own answer or self-generated evidence before presenting the external evidence changes receptiveness and induces confirmation bias toward the elicited prior. That is commit-then-consult, measured, with the same causal story (prior commitment resists override), differing only in that the evidence is a retrieved document rather than a distilled experience item. Longpre et al. 2021 (entity-based knowledge conflicts), Zhou et al. 2023 (context-faithful prompting, opinion-based framing to reduce over-reliance on context) and GenRead (Yu et al. 2023, generate-then-read) surround the same finding. Combined with CoVe, which the proposal concedes, this makes A2 a port of an established RAG effect into the agent-memory setting rather than a new causal lever. What is not clearly anticipated is P4, the ordering x instruction-optimization interaction; that is where the novelty actually lives, and it is the least-powered arm.
reviews.strongest_objection: P1, the headline and self-declared best-powered endpoint, is close to true by construction. In A2, pass 1 is a no-memory run, and a break is scored against A0, which is also a no-memory run. An A2 agent that is merely draft-sticky converges on A0 and therefore on zero breaks, with no anchoring account required; the break-halving in P1 measures revision reluctance, not the mechanism. The only non-degenerate endpoint is P2, fix preservation, which the proposal itself concedes is detectable only to about 3 points, and which the cited pilot (bank fixed zero items) may render undefined, since the dev precheck can fail and the proposal states no contingency beyond reporting it. Second, and worse for the sharpest claim: P4 compares break proportions across arms with different reference accuracies. G0 will be more accurate than A0, so the pool of reference-correct instances available to be broken is larger under I-star, and an unconditional break proportion rises mechanically even if the per-item override probability is identical. The predicted 1.5x ratio and 3-point absolute gap are exactly the size a base-rate shift produces. Nothing in the analysis section conditions the break rate on the reference-correct subset, so the anti-synergy result as specified is confounded in the direction of the prediction. Third, G3 is described as isolating slot from order with the same directive content, but a budget-capped GEPA run merges only the surviving directives, so G3 varies slot, optimizer vetting, and content selection at once; G3 vs A1 cannot support the slot claim as written. Finally, the practical payoff is thin even on success: A7 (k=3) reportedly already eliminated the harm at half of A2's call cost, and if the bank fixes nothing, A0 dominates every memory arm, so the paper can win P1 and still recommend nothing.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Redefine every break endpoint conditionally, breaks divided by reference-correct instances, and run the P4 difference-in-differences on conditional flip probabilities, with G0 vs A0 accuracy reported alongside so the reader can see the base-rate shift is removed; without this P4 is uninterpretable. 2) Report A2 keep-rate and the A2-vs-A0 first-action agreement, and pre-register a floor: a draft-stickiness figure that would make P1 vacuous. 3) Make the dev precheck a hard gate with a stated fallback (a stronger bank, an environment where retrieved experience demonstrably fixes items, or an explicit demotion of the paper to a one-sided harm-reduction claim). 4) Manipulate directiveness instead of only annotating it: add an arm rewriting retrieved items imperative-to-declarative at fixed content, slot, order and token count. 5) Split G3 into slot-only (verbatim extracted directives appended to the instruction, no GEPA pass) and slot-plus-vetting. 6) Run I-star from at least three GEPA seeds; one draw cannot carry an interaction claim the authors already call the weakest arm. 7) Cite and position against the knowledge-conflict literature above.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. (a) A declarative-rewrite arm: the identical retrieved items rewritten from imperative to descriptive/episodic form, injected memory-first at matched tokens. This is the only direct manipulation of the proposal's central construct, instruction-shaped content in the demonstration slot; as the grid stands, directiveness is purely observational (an annotation regression) and A6 rewrites for query relevance, not for grammatical mood, so it does not substitute. (b) A GEPA run with memory in the loop, producing an instruction optimized against the memory-first context. That is the composition the track actually asks about and the natural comparator for anti-synergy; as specified, I-star is optimized memory-free and then deployed with memory, so any G1 degradation is equally explained by instruction-context mismatch rather than by a stronger prior being abandoned. A slot-only routing condition without GEPA vetting is a third, needed to decontaminate G3.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above the median for effort and unusually honest, but not sufficient. It names specific IDs, gives per-item collide/no-collide verdicts, concedes CoVe as a structural ancestor after reviewer pressure, and self-reports an unfinished sweep. Two problems. First, the admitted gap sits exactly on the load-bearing claim: the authors themselves assign nontrivial probability to a draft-then-consult ordering ablation existing in an OpenReview or ACL/EMNLP appendix, and they did not look. An unsearched region containing the paper's main intervention is a weakness, not a neutral. Second, an entire relevant cluster is absent: nothing in the check covers knowledge-conflict RAG (Xie et al. ICLR 2024, Longpre et al. 2021, context-faithful prompting, GenRead), where the effect of eliciting a model's own answer before showing conflicting evidence is close to established; searching only agent-memory venues will not surface it. Citation hygiene also slips, Astute RAG and Madam-RAG are merged under 2504.13079 when they are separate papers with separate IDs, which lowers confidence in the rest of the ID list. Net: I did not find a preprint that already makes the P4 anti-synergy claim, and I judge that part plausibly unclaimed; the A2 ordering claim is not established as novel by this check.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That the harm from injected agent memory is caused by commitment *order* rather than volume or content — demonstrated by a token-matched intervention (log a memory-free draft, then revise against the identical retrieved items) — plus the risky corollary that GEPA-optimized instructions make memory-first injection more harmful, not less.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The collision check covers the 2026 agent-memory cluster well but is blind to the knowledge-conflict RAG literature, where the exact manipulation already exists. Xie et al., 'Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of LLMs in Knowledge Conflicts' (ICLR 2024) explicitly compares presenting conflicting external evidence cold versus after eliciting the model's own parametric answer, and reports a confirmation-bias/anchoring effect — i.e. that a prior commitment changes whether the model abandons its own answer. That is A1 vs. A2 in a non-agentic setting. Longpre et al. 2021 (entity-substitution conflict) and the generate-then-read line (GenRead, COMBO, Astute RAG 2504.13079) round out the same idea. Astute RAG is conceded and implemented as A5, which is good; Xie et al. is not cited at all, and it is the work that makes 'a logged pre-retrieval commitment reduces override' a confirmation rather than a discovery. What survives as new is narrower than the abstract claims: the agent-loop instantiation, the token-matched fix/break decomposition, and the P4 interaction with prompt optimization.
reviews.strongest_objection: P4, the proposal's self-declared sharpest and only unclaimed contribution, is confounded by construction. 'Break' is defined as right→wrong relative to a matched no-memory reference (A0 for the base arm, G0 for the coupling arm), but the plan reports break counts/rates over all 600 instances rather than over the at-risk set (instances the matched reference got right). If I* raises no-memory accuracy at all — which G0 exists to show it does — then G0 has a strictly larger pool of correct answers available to be broken, so the break count rises mechanically with zero change in the agent's propensity to override. The difference-in-differences (G1−G0) vs. (A1−A0) therefore mixes a real anchoring interaction with an at-risk-base-rate artifact, and the mixed-effects logistic model with a memory×optimization product term inherits the same problem unless it is fit on the at-risk subset. The prediction is stated as a ≥1.5× ratio and ≥3 absolute points precisely in the range that a 10-point accuracy gain from I* could partly manufacture. Secondarily: the same denominator issue means a *positive* P4 result cannot distinguish 'optimization amplifies anchoring' from 'optimization gives memory more to break,' which is the anti-synergy claim's entire content.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Redefine every break endpoint as a rate conditional on the matched no-memory reference being correct, and re-derive the P1 and P4 power analyses on that at-risk denominator; report raw counts beside it. (2) Run at least three independent GEPA searches for I* with different seeds and treat run as a random effect — the proposal admits I* is a single draw, and a one-draw interaction claim will not survive review whatever its sign. (3) Add the co-optimized arm (GEPA run *with* memory-first injection in the loop), which is the composition the track actually asks about; the current I* is optimized memory-free, so P4 tests a strawman deployment that no practitioner using GEPA+memory would build. (4) Precheck the *break* rate on the dev split, not only the ≥4% fix rate, and pre-register the contingency if A1 breaks fall near the pilot's handful rather than the assumed 60/600. (5) Make A2-vs-A0 net accuracy at matched call budget a primary, powered endpoint, not a secondary one. (6) Add the knowledge-conflict literature to the collision check and reposition the ordering result as a replication-plus-extension.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. The load-bearing omission is a GEPA run with memory in the loop (instructions optimized against the memory-first context, so the instruction can learn to caveat or subordinate retrieved experience). Without it, G1's anti-synergy is measured on a composition nobody deploys, and the obvious practitioner remedy is untested — it could erase the effect entirely. The cheap omission is a zero-cost framing control: memory-first, k=7, identical items, but each item wrapped as descriptive episodic evidence ('in a past episode the agent did X, outcome Y') with an instruction that retrieved experience is evidence and may be disregarded. That separates 'directive framing' from 'commitment order' at no extra compute, and it is exactly what the paper's own directiveness covariate implies should work. A6 (query-conditioned rewriting) is not a substitute — it changes item content, not imperative framing. If de-imperativized framing matches A2, the two-pass apparatus and its 2x call cost are unjustified.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average for this exercise and clearly not a rubber stamp: it names specific recent IDs (2601.22436, 2603.00026, 2603.02473, 2607.28272, 2604.27003, 2607.13591, 2606.05684, 2603.18272), gives a per-item collide/no-collide verdict with a reason, converts two near-collisions into run conditions (A5, A6), and volunteers a genuine limitation of the mirror-image finding (2601.22436) against P6. The self-declared gap — no OpenReview/ACL-EMNLP sweep for 'ordering ablation' appendices — is honest and I share the estimate that a draft-then-consult ordering plausibly appears as an appendix ablation somewhere. The substantive failure is scope, not effort: every cluster searched is agent-memory or prompt-optimization, and none is knowledge-conflict RAG, which is where the ordering manipulation has actually been run (Xie et al. ICLR 2024; Longpre et al. 2021; the generate-then-read line). A novelty claim built on 'nobody manipulates when the agent commits' cannot stand while that literature is unsearched. I found no preprint making the P4 anti-synergy claim, and I accept that piece as currently unclaimed — which is why the paper's novelty now rests almost entirely on its least-powered and most confounded arm.
